BiblicalUsage: A root can be a curse or a promise: Moses warns of a root that bears gall and wormwood among the people, and the prophets promise a remnant that will take root downward and bear fruit upward. Deborah's song even calls Ephraim a root that struck against Amalek, and Job pictures a man whose roots wrap around the heap.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe roots decide what a life becomes, because what is planted deep shows itself in the open. I hold that the only safe rooting is the one Isaiah promised, the root of Jesse, and everything else turns bitter in the end.
